children: Amid increased concern about artificial intelligence and its implications on humanity, Microsoft
co-founder Bill Gates is set to throw his hat into the ring, warning about its power.
Gates, set to appear on “Meet The Press,” will state that the technology is “powerful enough” to help cause at least 1B human deaths.

“AI is certainly powerful enough, to drive events, that you know, cause a billion deaths,” Gates said in a clip released on Friday by the long-standing NBC show. “So even though it's pretty hard to get to 100%, there's never been a weapon as powerful as the combination of people with ill intent using the latest AI tools.”

Gates added that he believes lawmakers and law enforcement need to get involved to help regulate AI and that self-regulation is not enough. “And it will be a little bit of overhead for the industry, but not a dramatic slowing of what they're doing.”
The 70-year-old Gates is among the most prominent technologists who have called on legislators to help regulate the industry. His comments come after Anthropic
CEO Dario Amodei called on the AI industry to “slow the pace” of AI model improvements.
OpenAI
CEO Sam Altman and SpaceX
CEO Elon Musk, both of whom compete with Anthropic,
with Amodei's comments and said the industry needs to slow down.
Microsoft
AI chief Mustafa Suleyman
with the trio and said competition with China should not prevent the United States from establishing safeguards for AI.
Their comments come after former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon
and said the companies are gambling with the future of humanity. “The people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade,” Coxon warned.
Evan Hubinger, Alignment Science Lead at Anthropic

, responded to Coxon and agreed. “I personally think it is >10% within the next decade,” he said, adding Anthropic does not have a plan to solve alignment for superintelligence yet. Alignment is the process of ensuring AI models' behavior matches human values and goals.
On the flip side of the debate are Meta Platforms
CEO Mark Zuckerberg and Nvidia
CEO Jensen Huang, both of whom have pushed back on the need to slow down.

President Trump has also rejected the need for the AI industry to slow down, citing competition with China. “We’re leading China in AI. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world, and frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI wins,” Trump told reporters earlier this month. “And we can put guardrails. We can do this and that. But I think you have a lot of negative forces that are bringing it up that shouldn’t be bringing it up.”

Trump is planning to appoint an “AI czar” who will help monitor the industry and introduce new safeguards and practices. On Friday, President Trump said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent would not be the AI czar, despite some speculation that he was interested in the position.

title: Bill Gates warns AI is 'powerful enough' to cause a billion deaths
